name: Palo Alto Networks
evidence_summary: Official sources describe Prisma SASE as converging cloud security, SD-WAN and digital experience management.
cost_model: Quote-based subscriptions; appliance/ION and Prisma Access/SASE licensing typically priced by users, bandwidth, locations and term.
key_differentiators: Prisma SASE converges SD-WAN, cloud-delivered security, and digital experience management (ADEM) under a single platform identity.
Strong threat intelligence and security capability inheritance from the wider Palo Alto Networks portfolio.
Often selected by buyers consolidating from multiple security vendors onto a single SASE platform.
best_fit_for: Enterprises with mature security operations that want SASE built around a leading security platform rather than a security layer on top of an SD-WAN platform.
Buyers consolidating CASB, SWG, ZTNA and FWaaS onto one vendor for unified policy.
Organisations with global SaaS-heavy traffic patterns that benefit from Prisma Access PoP coverage.
watch_outs: Premium pricing relative to firewall-led SD-WAN vendors; commercial model requires careful scoping by users, bandwidth, locations and term.
Managed delivery is via partners (Orange Business, NTT, others); first-party managed service is not the primary model.
Private global backbone is not vendor-owned; cloud transport uses internet and Prisma Access PoPs.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: Precision AI, AIOps for SASE and Strata Copilot.

resilience.note: Prisma Access multi-region redundancy; ION edge devices deploy in HA pairs.

profile.platform_architecture: Palo Alto Networks delivers SASE as Prisma SASE: Prisma SD-WAN (formerly CloudGenix) ION appliances at the edge and Prisma Access providing cloud-delivered security from compute in 100+ locations on Google Cloud and AWS. Prisma SD-WAN is application-defined, using app-level SLAs rather than tunnel-centric routing, with Strata Cloud Manager unifying management. AIOps for SASE provides predictive monitoring across the stack.
profile.security_sase: Security depth is the headline: ZTNA 2.0 with continuous inspection, SWG, CASB, DLP and FWaaS inherit two decades of Palo Alto firewall and threat research, with Precision AI applied across detection. Policy follows the user across branch, remote and data centre via one security model. For security-led procurement, capability per feature is consistently at the top of the market.
profile.service_support_channel: Direct enterprise sales plus a strong partner bench; managed Prisma SASE is available through global carriers including Orange, Verizon and NTT and UK security MSPs. Professional services and Unit 42 incident expertise back deployment. Operating the platform DIY suits mature security teams; many UK mid-market buyers take it via an MSP wrapper.
profile.commercials_verdict: Licensing is per user for Prisma Access plus appliance subscriptions for Prisma SD-WAN, quote based and at premium positioning. The Netify verdict: shortlist Palo Alto when security architecture leads the decision, when ZTNA depth and DLP capability carry board weight, or when consolidating onto an existing Strata or Cortex estate. Budget-led, network-first projects often find better value elsewhere.

vendor_faqs.q: What makes Prisma SD-WAN different from tunnel-based SD-WAN?
vendor_faqs.a: ION appliances make forwarding decisions per application against app-level SLAs rather than per tunnel, which simplifies policy for SaaS-heavy estates and feeds clean telemetry into AIOps. The trade-off is a smaller routing feature set than router-heritage rivals, so validate complex topologies.

vendor_faqs.q: Is Prisma Access a true ZTNA solution?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes. ZTNA 2.0 applies continuous trust verification and deep inspection after connection, not just at connect time, covering private apps, SaaS and web from one policy. It is among the strongest ZTNA implementations on the market.

vendor_faqs.q: Can Prisma SASE be consumed as a managed service?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes, through global providers such as Orange Business, Verizon and NTT, and through UK security MSPs. Managed routes suit buyers who want Palo Alto capability without operating Strata Cloud Manager in-house.

shortlist_summary: Palo Alto Networks offer Prisma SASE, converging SD-WAN, cloud-delivered security and digital experience management (ADEM) under a single platform identity, with security depth that goes well beyond most SD-WAN-first platforms. Typically shortlisted by organisations where security capability and application performance visibility are both weighted heavily, rather than those primarily looking to replace an MPLS estate.
cost_note: Per-user Prisma Access plus appliance subscriptions at premium positioning; buyers pay for security depth.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK Prisma Access presence; delivered direct or via UK partners and carriers.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: With Prisma Access, Palo Alto Networks deploys and manages the security infrastructure globally to secure your remote networks and mobile users.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Palo Alto Networks operates the cloud security infrastructure itself, but end-to-end design, change, support and reporting for a customer is positioned as an MSP function. The Managed Prisma SASE blog (source 13) describes the fully managed model as one where the MSP is responsible for all aspects of the tenant service lifecycle including security policy configuration and operations, and the Managed SASE page (source 6) frames fully managed and co-managed delivery as something MSPs provide using the platform. Graded managed_service_dependent rather than yes because the provider of the wrap is a partner, not Palo Alto Networks.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: The MSP provides delegated access to the customer to co-manage the policies and their specific services.
f03_co_managed_service.note: Co-management is explicitly described as an MSP-delivered model in which the MSP delegates policy rights to the customer. The platform supplies the delegated administration mechanism; the service relationship sits with the MSP, so graded managed_service_dependent. Source 13 is dated 4 April 2022 and may be superseded.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: MSPs can securely delegate responsibilities while ensuring only authorized users can read or modify critical security configurations.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Hierarchical multitenancy and granular role-based delegated administration are evidenced on the Managed SASE page (source 6) and the 2022 MSP press release (source 14), which describes a cloud-based management portal with hierarchical multitenancy using granular role-based access control. Graded partial rather than yes because no evidence of branded or white-label portals and service templates carrying the MSP's own brand was found on the pages reviewed; the Prisma SASE for MSPs datasheet (source 18) is gated and returned no usable text.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: Palo Alto Networks manages sizing, content versioning, monitoring, upgrades, and security subscriptions.
f07_lifecycle_management.note: For the cloud service and for SASE Private Location, Palo Alto Networks handles sizing, content versioning, upgrades and security subscriptions as part of the service. Graded partial because hardware replacement and RMA, ION appliance firmware handling, renewals and end-of-life planning were not evidenced: the Support Policies page (source 19) is a link index that returned no substantive text, and no RMA or end-of-life policy document was read in this task.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: The cellular ION devices have integrated 4G or 5G cellular modem for primary or backup WAN connectivity.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: Documentation confirms integrated 4G and 5G modems usable as primary or backup transport, optional dual SIMs for carrier failover, automatic carrier profile and firmware detection for AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon, and separate primary and backup APN and circuit label configuration. Cellular statistics and SIM operations pages exist in the same documentation set but were not opened in this task, so signal monitoring is indicated by the documentation structure rather than quoted.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: With Prisma Access, Palo Alto Networks deploys and manages the security infrastructure globally to secure your remote networks and mobile users.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: The PoPs are Palo Alto Networks' own service, sold under its own brand and covered by its own SLA, so this is yes rather than partner_integrated. Recorded for transparency: the compute those PoPs run on is rented from GCP and AWS (source 11), which is a hosting arrangement rather than reselling another vendor's SASE gateway service.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: SASE Private Location enables you to deploy Prisma Access services within your own infrastructure.
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: SASE Private Location is a customer-hosted deployment of Prisma Access services on the customer's own hypervisor and ISP links, with Palo Alto Networks retaining backend management. Corroborated by the sovereignty blog (source 12), which states that for organisations with the most stringent data residency requirements Palo Alto offers SASE Private Location. Colo-Connect (source 9) is a different thing: private connectivity into the shared cloud, not a dedicated PoP.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Prisma SASE leverages the infrastructure of major hyperscale providers such as Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Amazon Web Services (AWS).
f21_private_global_backbone.note: Inter-region transport rides the backbones of Google Cloud and AWS rather than a network owned or controlled by Palo Alto Networks. The same post adds that Prisma SASE benefits from private peering connections between tier 1 cloud providers and other public cloud platforms, SaaS networks and ISPs, which again describes third-party peering. Colo-Connect (source 9) uses GCP interconnect technology, reinforcing the same conclusion. No evidence of Palo Alto-owned fibre, wavelengths or core routing was found.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: If, during any calendar month, the Service availability falls below 99.999%, Customer can submit a claim for credit
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: The published SLA is contractual with service credits and covers three separate measures: service availability at 99.999%, a Monthly Security Processing Latency Percentage at 99.99% and a Monthly SaaS Application Latency Percentage at 99.99%, with credits scaling to 100% where availability falls below 98%. That goes beyond best-effort targets. Support response times and change handling commitments were not evidenced in the SLA text reviewed.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Threat prevention, malware prevention, URL filtering, SSL decryption, and application-based policy capabilities are built-in to provide you with the same level of security no matter where your users are or what resources they are accessing.
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: All the inspection functions in the definition are built into the Prisma Access platform and are Palo Alto Networks' own technology (App-ID, Threat Prevention, WildFire, Advanced URL Filtering), not a third party's, so this is yes rather than partner_integrated. Stateful firewalling is inherent to the PAN-OS engine the service runs on but is not named in the quoted sentence.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Discover sensitive data wherever it resides and travels.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Enterprise DLP is a first-party Palo Alto Networks product delivered as part of the SASE portfolio. The same page also states comprehensive coverage for data in-motion and at-rest, classification using thousands of data identifiers and over 100 trainable ML classifiers, and real-time user coaching and adaptive response. Confidence is medium rather than high because the page is written in marketing register and does not document alerting or exception and incident approval workflows explicitly; no Enterprise DLP administration documentation was read in this task.

f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. I looked at the Managed SASE page (source 6), the Managed Prisma SASE blog (source 13), the Support Policies page (source 19) and the Prisma Access administration documentation (source 3). Palo Alto Networks operates the cloud platform and backs it with a 99.999% availability SLA, and the MSP blog refers to operational lifecycle management that includes monitoring and reporting, but no Palo Alto-operated 24/7 NOC and SOC owning customer incidents through to root cause analysis with structured service reviews and change governance is documented for Prisma SASE. On the material reviewed that wrap appears to sit with MSP partners, but no quotable sentence stating it was found, so this is recorded as unknown rather than graded.

delivery_model.quote: With Prisma Access, Palo Alto Networks deploys and manages the security infrastructure globally to secure your remote networks and mobile users.
delivery_model.note: Palo Alto Networks authors and operates the Prisma SASE cloud platform (Prisma Access, Prisma SD-WAN, Enterprise DLP) and runs the underlying security infrastructure, but the customer-facing fully managed and co-managed wrap is positioned as something managed service providers deliver on top of the platform (Managed SASE page and the Managed Prisma SASE blog). Consulting and deployment services are sold directly, but no Palo Alto-operated managed SASE service offering was found on the pages reviewed.

underlay_ownership.quote: You provide the hypervisor, ISP links, and public IP address infrastructure.
underlay_ownership.note: No evidence that Palo Alto Networks owns or resells physical circuits. For SASE Private Location the customer supplies the ISP links and compute; for the shared cloud service the compute and inter-region transport are rented from GCP and AWS (source 11); Colo-Connect uses GCP interconnect (source 9). Prisma SD-WAN is transport-agnostic over customer-procured WAN and cellular links. Graded customer_supplied_only rather than mixed because nothing found indicates Palo Alto sells connectivity itself, though the absence of a circuit-sales page is not proof, hence medium confidence.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Threat prevention, malware prevention, URL filtering, SSL decryption, and application-based policy capabilities are built-in to provide you with the same level of security no matter where your users are or what resources they are accessing.
sse_layer_ownership.note: The security service edge stack is Palo Alto Networks' own engineering: PAN-OS-derived inspection delivered from Prisma Access, with Enterprise DLP as a first-party product (source 15). No third-party SSE vendor is named anywhere in the material reviewed. The hosting substrate is GCP and AWS, but that is infrastructure rental, not a resold security stack.

regulatory_documentation.quote: The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) is a U.S. Federal Government-wide program that provides a standardized approach to the security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring of cloud products and services.
regulatory_documentation.note: The trust centre names specific attestations rather than making a general assurance statement: FedRAMP, StateRAMP, SOC 2+, PCI DSS, ISMAP, IRAP, TISAX, Germany C5, CSA STAR, Common Criteria, FIPS 140, Cyber Essentials Plus, NCSC Cloud Security Principles, ENS, DODIN APL and an ISO certifications section. Frameworks I looked for and did NOT find named on this page: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2, and the exact string ISO 27001 (the page refers to ISO certifications generically and to the ISO 27000 series). SOC 2 appears only in the form SOC 2+.

pop_count.quote: Prisma Access provides over 100 locations worldwide
pop_count.note: The supplier publishes a floor, not an exact figure, so the value is recorded as 100+. The same documentation page enumerates compute locations by region across Africa, Asia, ANZ, Europe, Japan, Middle East, North America and South America, plus separate lists for Explicit Proxy, Colo-Connect, High Performance Remote Networks, Secure Agentless Access and Local Zones, but prints no consolidated total. The page is undated so the figure is point-in-time. Confidence is medium because a range claim cannot be resolved to a single number.

sla_availability_pct.quote: If, during any calendar month, the Service availability falls below 99.999%, Customer can submit a claim for credit
sla_availability_pct.note: Taken from the published contractual SLA document rather than a marketing page. Corroborated by the Prisma Access product page, which advertises 99.999% industry-leading uptime SLAs, and by the architecture blog. Separate 99.99% commitments apply to security processing latency and third-party SaaS application latency; those are latency percentages, not availability, so they are not used for this field.

sectors.energy_utilities.note: Two dedicated industry pages exist, electric utilities and oil and gas, which meets the dedicated industry page test. Confidence is held at medium rather than high because neither page names an individual utility or energy customer, so the grade rests on vendor pages and the unaudited about us claims '10 of 10 Largest utilities in the world' and '6 of 10 Largest oil & gas in the world' rather than on a verifiable named reference. No energy-sector SASE or SD-WAN case study was found.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Palo Alto Networks achieves FedRAMP High Authorization across network, cloud and security operations.
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Strongest sector evidence in this record. A published accreditation, FedRAMP High, plus DoD Impact Level 5, DoDIN APL and Commercial Solutions for Classified, all independently checkable against US government registers. Supported by a dedicated public sector page naming Vallejo Flood and Wastewater District, and by Ministry of Justice and Vermont Judiciary on the SASE customer stories index. The 25 plus UK G-Cloud listings [32] evidence public sector routes to market in the UK as well.

sectors.education.quote: Discover how Palo Alto Networks trusted platforms and proven expertise safeguard public sector organizations — federal, K–12, higher education, and state and local government.
sectors.education.note: A dedicated education industry page exists at /industry/education headed 'Securely Connecting Students', which satisfies the dedicated industry page test, and the customers index carries both Education and Higher Education filter facets. Confidence is medium not high because no named education customer could be retrieved from either page. One partner G-Cloud listing [33] separately states 'Education pricing available', which suggests a sector-specific commercial motion but is a reseller statement, not the supplier's.

sectors.transport_logistics.note: The only evidence is that 'Transportation' and 'Airlines' exist as industry filter facets on the supplier's customer index. There is no dedicated transport or logistics industry page in the industries index [3], and no named transport or logistics customer could be retrieved because the customer index is JavaScript paginated and rendered only five cards. Graded partial rather than yes on that basis; a facet implies at least one listed customer but shows nothing about capability. Grupo Bimbo is described on the SASE page as protecting a global connected supply chain across 35 countries, but it is labelled Manufacturing on the customers index, so I have not counted it here.

sectors.professional_services.quote: Prisma Browser delivered true zero trust security to the last mile. It strengthened, complemented, and augmented our SASE strategy for hybrid workforce and workplace.
sectors.professional_services.note: Named case study for Wipro, industry labelled 'IT and Consulting', region Global, and the customers index carries a 'Professional & Legal Services' facet. Confidence is medium because the deployed product is Prisma Browser rather than Prisma Access or Prisma SD-WAN, although the customer quote explicitly places it inside their SASE strategy. There is no dedicated professional services industry page.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: Just three members of our network team deployed 400 Prisma SD-WAN Instant-On Network (ION) devices to locations scattered throughout the country in only 12 months.
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: American Food & Vending is a named Prisma SASE and Prisma SD-WAN case study labelled Hospitality, United States, 2,000 employees. This is a directly relevant SD-WAN reference rather than a general platform one. The customers index also carries a Hospitality facet. Confidence is medium because it is a single reference and there is no dedicated hospitality industry page; Green Bay Packers and Village Roadshow sit under Sports & Leisure and Media & Entertainment respectively and were not counted here.

regions.uk_ireland.note: Graded partner_integrated, not yes, because every piece of UK evidence found is partner delivered. The UK Government Digital Marketplace carries 25 plus live G-Cloud listings of Prisma Access, all from UK resellers such as Khipu Networks, Softcat, Computacenter, CDW, Bytes, Trustmarque, boxxe and Phoenix Software, not from Palo Alto Networks itself. Nuffield Health, a UK healthcare provider, appears on the healthcare page but the page does not state a country. The supplier's own UK domain [31] publishes no UK service delivery, data residency or framework statement, and no vendor-published UK point of presence list could be retrieved. Ireland: the only Ireland evidence found is a Dublin office on the locations page [16], which the brief excludes.

regions.europe.quote: In addition to the data residency controls we provide customers for all of our cloud services, Sovereign Cortex with T Security provides additional sovereign controls for every layer of the environment.
regions.europe.note: Dated release of 9 June 2026, datelined Amsterdam and Munich. The quoted sentence is a supplier claim of data residency controls across all its cloud services, and the same release states 'all support personnel are based exclusively in Europe, and all contractual agreements are governed by European law' and names GDPR, NIS2 and DORA. Caveat to record: the exclusively-European support and governing law commitments attach to the Sovereign Cortex with T Security offering delivered with Deutsche Telekom, not to Prisma SASE generally. VINCI, headquartered in France, corroborates European delivery but on Cortex XDR rather than SASE.

regions.north_america.quote: Palo Alto Networks achieves FedRAMP High Authorization across network, cloud and security operations.
regions.north_america.note: FedRAMP High plus DoD Impact Level 5 authorisation is service availability evidence for the United States, not merely a sales presence, and is checkable against US government registers. Corroborated by two United States SASE and SD-WAN case studies, Westfield (19 malls) and American Food & Vending (400 ION devices). Canada: the only Canadian evidence found is a Toronto office on the locations page [16], which the brief excludes, so Canada specifically is weaker than the United States.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: A lean two-person security team at Zespri completed the implementation in under six months
regions.asia_pacific.note: Two named Prisma SASE customer deployments in the region, Zespri in New Zealand and Village Roadshow in Australia, are direct service delivery evidence. The locations page separately describes Singapore as 'headquarters for supporting our business and customers in Asia Pacific (APAC)', but that is an office and is not relied on for the grade. Confidence is medium because no vendor-published Asia Pacific point of presence or availability list could be retrieved; both references are Australia and New Zealand, with nothing found for Japan, India or South East Asia beyond offices.

regions.middle_east_africa.note: No service delivery evidence found. Checked the Prisma Access product page, the Prisma SD-WAN page, the Prisma Access and Prisma SASE datasheet pages, the SASE and SASE customer stories pages, the technical documentation index and the press release index, and found no Middle East or Africa point of presence, coverage or availability statement and no named customer in the region. The locations page lists offices in Qatar (Doha), Saudi Arabia (Riyadh), UAE (Dubai) and South Africa (Johannesburg), but the Netify definition explicitly excludes sales offices, so those are recorded as context only and carry no grade.

regions.latin_america.note: Insufficient evidence to grade. Grupo Bimbo, a Mexico headquartered group, is presented on the SASE page as protecting its global connected supply chain across 35 countries and appears on the customers index labelled Manufacturing, which points towards Latin American delivery, but three candidate case study URLs all returned HTTP 404 so no country or coverage statement could be confirmed and no verbatim quote could be captured. The locations page lists Brazil (São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro) and Mexico (Mexico City) offices, which the brief excludes. Recorded as unknown rather than partial because no quotable delivery statement was obtained.

regions.china_mainland.note: The supplier's technical documentation index carries a dedicated 'Prisma Access China' topic, which is China-specific rather than a generic global claim and is why this is graded partial rather than unknown. However the topic page itself could not be opened: five candidate URLs across documentation versions all returned HTTP 404, so the licensing arrangement, local partner and any restrictions remain unverified. Treat as an indication that a distinct mainland China offering exists, not as confirmation of its terms. Offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Macau appear on the locations page but are excluded by the brief. A buyer should request the China documentation and the specific licensed arrangement directly.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: The about us stat block also carries '70K+ Customers Globally', '8 of 10 Largest U.S. banks', '10 of 10 Largest utilities in the world', '6 of 10 Largest oil & gas in the world' and '7 of 10 Top U.S. hospitals'. These are unaudited vendor claims, but they are explicit and the supporting case studies are consistent with them: VINCI at 200,000 endpoints across a group operating in 120 plus countries, Grupo Bimbo across 35 countries, Wipro, Autodesk and Colgate-Palmolive. Every SASE case study located is a large or upper mid enterprise.

organisation_fit.mid_market.note: No evidence of explicit mid-market targeting found. Checked the SASE page, Prisma Access page, Prisma SD-WAN page, both datasheet landing pages and the press release index for mid-market, midsize or SMB tiering, a mid-market product edition, or mid-market pricing, and found none. Two managed service and MSP partner page URLs were tried and both returned HTTP 404, so a partner-led mid-market motion could not be checked. Circumstantially the smaller named references sit in this bracket, American Food & Vending at 2,000 employees and Cordis at 2,500 employees, but neither is described by the supplier as a mid-market customer, and inferring a mid-market tier from customer headcount would be exactly the guesswork this exercise replaces.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: flexible and accessible pricing for any small business
organisation_fit.small_business.note: Graded partial rather than yes, and the distinction matters for a SASE and SD-WAN comparison. There is unambiguous, dated small business targeting: a press release of 23 March 2026 headed 'Palo Alto Networks Introduces the Most Secure Workspace for Small Business', describing a product that lets 'small business owners to easily configure and manage the apps and AI tools their business relies on'. But the product is Prisma Browser for Business, an adjacent secure browser offering, not Prisma Access or Prisma SD-WAN. The release states 'Prisma Browser for Business is available today in the United States. Start the 30-day free trial', so availability at launch is United States only. No small business tier, entry point or pricing was found anywhere in the SASE or SD-WAN portfolio, and no small business definition by headcount or revenue is published.

published_pricing.note: The supplier publishes no pricing of its own: the Prisma Access page, Prisma SD-WAN page and both datasheet landing pages were checked and contain no price, no entry point and no packaging detail. The grade therefore rests on third party listed pricing on the UK Government Digital Marketplace, a mandatory-price procurement register, combined with the supplier's own positioning language on the Prisma SASE datasheet page, 'the industry's most comprehensive secure access service edge (SASE) solution'. CONFLICT TO RECORD, not resolved: two resellers list materially different prices for nominally the same product. Khipu Networks lists Palo Alto Networks Prisma Access (SASE) at '£68.86 a user' with 'Education pricing available'; Softcat lists Palo Alto Prisma Access at '£90 a unit', where 'a unit' is undefined and may not be per user. Both are reseller-set UK channel prices under G-Cloud and neither is the supplier's list price. Confidence is medium: the direction of travel is clearly premium, consistent with an enterprise platform sold to Fortune 10 accounts with no published small business or mid-market SASE tier, but the underlying figures are indicative rather than authoritative and a buyer should treat them as a starting point for negotiation, not a quote.

conflicts.claim_a: Prisma Access provides over 100 locations worldwide
conflicts.claim_b: The same documentation page enumerates only roughly 70 distinct entries in its compute locations table and prints no consolidated total, so the enumerated detail does not visibly reconcile to the headline over 100 figure unless the specialty location lists are counted as well

conflicts.claim_b: Prisma SASE leverages the infrastructure of major hyperscale providers such as Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Amazon Web Services (AWS).
